title: Prevent idle fan stall after CX7 hotplug powers down on standalone DGX Spark
failure: A DGX Spark FE P4242 A04 (DGX OS 7.6.0, BIOS 5.36_0ACUM027, driver 580.178.04) reportedly powers down an uncabled ConnectX-7 via mtk_pcie_hotplug about 16 seconds after boot, followed by stopped fans and dangerous idle heat. The author reports a reversible module-block workaround; about 17 W added consumption is cited from another thread, not a local measurement.
current_coverage: Blackbox records temperatures and documents that standard hwmon/NVML paths do not expose fan RPM (FEATURE-FAN-RPM done). It cannot verify fan rotation or correlate CX7 hotplug removal with a subsequent fan stall.
gap_or_complement: Prefer an OEM-supported firmware/driver fix. On identified lab hardware, test an opt-in, reversible workaround that prevents CX7 removal, with temperature/PCIe/network controls and predeclared soak. Never default the module block or claim safety from low GPU power or healthy field diagnostics alone.
evidence_level: medium: complete 19-post textual thread, repeated headless/idle symptoms and a single author's five-unit comparison/workaround; causal mechanism and cross-OEM behavior remain unconfirmed. Binary attachments were not inspected.
risks: Keeping CX7 powered may add roughly 17 W per the author-cited separate report and change network/power behavior.
A module blacklist may prevent supported fabric operation or firmware diagnostics.
The fan does not expose a standard RPM signal, so temperature stability alone can miss a transient stall.
Never deploy a temporary module suspension without a named watcher, expiry and verified restore; retain the file by rename and record sha256/mode.
closure: Obtain vendor disposition for the exact OEM/BIOS/EC/driver stack or run matched repeated A/B tests of CX7 present/removed and hotplug active/blocked in headless idle, DPMS, load and thermal soak. Capture PCIe presence, kernel logs, temperatures, external power, network health, elapsed time and rollback. Report all unavailable signals and stop on thermal limits.

title: Validate kernel, initramfs, signed modules and OTA pairing before reboot
failure: A DGX Spark update to kernel 7.0.0-1019 with driver 580.178.04/DKMS left no matching initrd and caused VFS root-mount panic; NVIDIA's signed prebuilt module replacement and dpkg/apt/initrd checks were confirmed as recovery. Separately, driver 580.173.02 on OTA2607 paired to 580.159.03 failed GSP secure boot on two DGX Spark; rerunning Dashboard update later fixed one report. NVIDIA also advised multi-node NCCL/RoCE owners to hold kernel 7.0.0-1019 and posted kho=off mitigation. Exact package/kernel/OTA pairing matters.
current_coverage: Blackbox records kernel/driver state after boot. Existing post-update and boot recovery tasks do not establish that the next kernel has an initrd and signed compatible GPU module, or that the driver matches the installed DGX OTA before reboot.
gap_or_complement: Prototype a read-only pre-reboot preflight for dpkg/apt consistency, target kernel image and nonempty initrd, signed module provider/secure-boot compatibility, known-good previous kernel, and NVIDIA OTA/kernel/driver pairing. Apply only vendor-confirmed matching package remediation; use the 383254 kho=off advice only on a matching affected multi-node stack. Preflight must also separate APT/package inconsistency from fwupd server/device update status: detect source-list parse errors or HTML served as a repo file, stale/no firmware metadata, and upstream rate-limit/download failure as distinct blocked states. Never auto-delete/replace repository definitions or reflash because the dashboard continues to show an update badge.
evidence_level: high for the reported missing-initrd failure and vendor recovery (user confirms); medium for OTA driver mismatch (two matching units, dashboard rerun resolution without a published root-cause correction) and advisory mitigation. The inspected local host has prebuilt LRM, no DKMS package, and initrds present, so it does not match the reported broken state.
risks: DKMS/module checks can false-positive on built-in modules or OEM-specific packaging.
Installing a mismatched driver or removing DKMS outside the named stack can break GPU or boot.
A previous kernel may be absent or incompatible with firmware; verify recovery before updates.
A workaround may regress NCCL/RoCE performance or security; measure and rollback on the exact multi-node stack.
Replacing or deleting an invalid APT source can change trusted package origins; preserve the file/hash and require an official architecture-specific repository URL/key before remediation.
closure: Create fixtures for incomplete dpkg, absent/empty initrd, valid prebuilt signed modules, DKMS conflict, Secure Boot, OTA driver mismatch and healthy negatives. Exercise an identified lab unit on a vendor-supported update, prove the gate runs before reboot, capture boot/GPU/NCCL health, and verify rollback to a bootable previous kernel. Keep exact OEM, OS, kernel, driver, BIOS/EC and package origin in evidence.

title: Detect unsupported nvidia-drm modeset override before DGX OS OTA
failure: A DGX Spark OTA 7.5.0 / driver 580.173.02 report lost all display outputs when NVIDIA's nvidia-drm-options-modeset0 package forced modeset=0. Removing the package/override, rebooting and power-cycling AC restored KMS and USB-C DP; the author reports a later OTA meta fix. Local host has package 25.07-1 and an override file but the effective modeset value could not be read, so local impact is unknown.
current_coverage: Blackbox remains operable headless and has no OTA preflight that validates DRM override compatibility with target driver/OTA or warns that the display path will disappear.
gap_or_complement: Use vendor/package compatibility declarations to warn or stop only the known incompatible update combination. Preserve SSH recovery and avoid automatically deleting modprobe configuration without a supported rollback.
evidence_level: medium: one detailed report with recovery and subsequent OTA fix; attachment was post-fix and not inspected. Local exposure is plausible but effective KMS mode could_not_run due permissions.
risks: Conflicting modprobe files may not reflect the effective runtime value.
An overbroad conflict rule could block a supported headless or alternate-display setup.
The display recovery required a full AC cycle and could interrupt workloads.
closure: Validate exact DGX OS/OTA/kernel/driver/package versions and effective KMS state on a lab DGX Spark; test direct HDMI, USB-C DP and hub with healthy and incompatible combinations, preserve SSH, and verify vendor-supported rollback and update behavior.

title: Detect USB-HID perdido tras actualización de kernel o driver
failure: A DGX Spark owner reports that after apt/dpkg repair and reboot the login screen worked but keyboard/mouse and SSH were unavailable; a second user reported usbhid/hid_generic reload as a workaround. Exact OS/kernel/driver cause was not established.
current_coverage: FEATURE-USB-XHCI-FORENSICS detects xHCI failures but does not distinguish absent HID modules/device from a live controller.
gap_or_complement: Check package/kernel update state and USB-HID availability while distinguishing headless systems, built-in modules and absent peripherals; do not autoload or reinstall modules without verifying the case.
evidence_level: medium: two textual reports, one with package repair sequence; exact versions and common cause are unknown.
risks: Headless systems and built-in drivers can resemble missing HID.
Blind module changes can disrupt USB/network input or make recovery worse.
closure: Fixture active, built-in, missing, no-device and broken-dpkg cases; safely exercise an identified lab update and demonstrate local/remote recovery and rollback.

title: Validate package graph integrity for critical DGX station packages
failure: An older DGX OS report says removing aisleriot would remove nvidia-system-station due to package dependency metadata; NVIDIA acknowledged the historical dependency and announced a fix.
current_coverage: Current inspected package graph has no direct aisleriot dependency; nvidia-system-station 2404.26.01-1 depends on station-core/common/utils and recommends games/apps/localization. The formerly reported package state is not present on the inspected host.
gap_or_complement: Keep the proposal at P3 and verify current package metadata/upstream fix before building any bespoke guard. Close as corrected upstream if an apt simulation proves removal no longer affects the critical meta-package.
evidence_level: high for the inspected local package graph; medium for historical forum report; no current local exposure demonstrated.
risks: A custom guard can become stale after upstream dependency corrections and block legitimate maintenance.
closure: Record apt-cache depends/simulated removal against the exact current DGX package versions and show either the corrected graph or a reproducible harmful removal plan; no bespoke guard without a current failing case.

title: Validate architecture-matched FlashInfer cubins and safe fallback for GB10 inference
failure: A DGX Spark owner reports system unresponsiveness requiring power cycle while serving Llama-4-Scout-17B NVFP4 via TRT-LLM 1.2.0rc4. A later NVIDIA/community response says FlashInfer MoE FP4 cubins published for SM100 fail on GB10 SM121 and recommends a Triton fallback for vLLM. This architecture diagnosis/workaround has not been reproduced on the original TRT-LLM command; attached logs were not inspected. A separate nanochat thread on GB10 reports Triton using CUDA 12.8 ptxas failing on `sm_121a`; one owner reports that PyTorch 2.9/Triton 3.5 plus CUDA Toolkit 13.0.2 ptxas allowed training to run. This is a distinct compile-toolchain path from FlashInfer cubin packaging, with no confirmation that toolkit install is safe for every DGX OS image. Other GB10 reports show PyTorch installed from CPU-only or incompatible CUDA wheel indices, wheel hash mismatch, and vLLM undefined CUTLASS SM100 symbols when building for a mismatched architecture list. These are workload build/runtime failures and do not prove host corruption.
current_coverage: Blackbox observes general GPU/memory/host failure signals. It does not validate that a workload/container kernel image includes cubins compatible with GB10 SM121 before launching.
gap_or_complement: Reproduce on a named GB10 OEM, kernel, driver, CUDA and TRT-LLM/vLLM container; determine whether incompatible cubin failure can actually hang/power-cycle the host or only fail a process. If confirmed, document an exact supported container or pre-launch architecture check and fallback (Triton where supported). For supported launches, inspect package metadata, CUDA build/available device, toolkit/PTXAS version and architecture list before loading a model. Never bypass a pip hash mismatch without checking the authoritative wheel hash; never copy a community CMake patch excluding architecture targets as a generic fix.
evidence_level: low-to-medium: one report of a power-cycle-requiring crash; root cause comes from a responder and may concern a different vLLM/FlashInfer execution path. No log/post-change confirmation. Thread 348537 has one detailed failure/workaround report and follow-up running progress, but the 20-minute crash in an earlier attempt remains unexplained; no independent reproduction.
risks: Changing backend may affect performance or model correctness.
An incompatible cubin may only cause application-level errors; treating it as host instability without reproduction would misdiagnose the outage.
The environment variable mentioned applies to vLLM MoE path, not automatically TRT-LLM.
Manual CUDA toolkit/package changes can conflict with DGX OS driver/toolkit ownership; require exact compatibility validation and rollback before any recommendation.
Wheel/hash or CMake workarounds can mask artifact corruption or remove required architecture kernels; validate against official package hashes and named device/toolchain before use.
closure: Inspect the linked log, reproduce the exact TRT-LLM workload on identified GB10, and compare the failing path with a supported Triton/backend build while recording process and host status. Verify model output, throughput, stability soak and rollback; otherwise close as unconfirmed application failure outside BB scope.

title: Detect and validate EEE link stalls on DGX Spark direct Ethernet
failure: On DGX Spark DGX OS 7.2.3/OTA 7.3.1, kernel 6.14.0-1015, Realtek r8127 11.014.00-NAPI and direct Windows11/Intel I225-V Ethernet, an owner reports link down/up and traffic stalls that interrupt SSH/Sync. Disabling EEE on enP7s7 stabilized that environment; a switch-connected Spark with EEE active was a negative control. Another Lenovo PGX owner reports the mitigation helped, without versions.
current_coverage: Current BB has network traffic and reachability observations and a separate Wi-Fi isolation card, but does not specifically record EEE negotiation or correlate r8127 link events with admin-path loss/recovery.
gap_or_complement: Run a matched EEE on/off A/B with exact OEM, kernel, r8127 version and link partner; preserve the switch-connected control. If confirmed, document an opt-in, interface-identity-bound mitigation and rollback for affected direct links; do not disable EEE globally.
evidence_level: medium: detailed post-update owner report and explicit manual workaround result; topology/Intel I225-V may be causal confound, and no independent reproduction on BB host.
risks: Global EEE disable changes power/latency behavior and can harm links that negotiate EEE correctly.
Interface names and partner EEE capabilities vary by OEM/topology.
NetworkManager/SSH absence alone cannot distinguish link failure, DHCP, routing or remote endpoint.
closure: Test exact Spark/Windows Intel I225-V direct link through repeated link/power cycles with EEE enabled and disabled; compare a stable switch control. Record link resets, EEE status, IPv4/IPv6, loss duration, SSH reconnect time and soak; check primary vendor guidance and demonstrate restoration of original EEE state.

title: Prevent an OOM-triggered Docker auto-restart loop from making DGX Spark unrecoverable
failure: A DGX Spark running Ubuntu24.04 is reported to freeze immediately after login when a Docker container auto-restarts. NVIDIA says a known OOM issue may be involved and recommends Safe Mode plus removing model files so the container cannot reload; exact kernel/driver/model limits and log signature are absent, and no follow-up confirms fix. Related reports show OOM during GPT-OSS-120B/65K load with NVRM `NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY`, transient UI stalls and an author-reported container workload crash/reboot; another multi-agent workload with the 120B model froze a Spark. One later report says a software update resolved the problem. These do not establish a single current OOM signature.
current_coverage: BB has memory/PSI/OOM and CUDA cgroup investigations; these can reveal pressure while the host remains responsive, but the thread describes a container restart path that may freeze the machine before the operator can collect state. One separate txt2kg example shows `unhealthy` due solely to an image healthcheck invoking absent `curl`; an operator installing the utility made it healthy. Distinguish healthcheck dependency/image drift and application port binding from OOM before restarting or escalating.
gap_or_complement: Use a bounded memory/cgroup budget and restart policy for known workloads; ensure an operator can disable the offending container from a recovery/safe boot without destroying its model/data. Confirm that the OOM event is actually recorded before assuming this is the forum case. Treat readiness by workload phase: model download, compile/CUDA-graph warmup and API-ready states can take many minutes (forum reports 15 minutes and an unresolved 90-minute dual-node warmup). Prefer explicit progress/readiness and bounded, workload-specific grace periods over restarting on a short socket timeout; only add this if a real BB restart/admission path can interrupt the warmup.
evidence_level: low-to-medium: host freeze and Docker restart are owner-reported; OOM relationship and Safe Mode workaround are NVIDIA support hypothesis/guidance, not a reproduced fix. One two-node vLLM case became healthy after ~15 minutes; one TRT-LLM dual-node CUDA-graph warmup remained unresolved after 90+ minutes with no host telemetry. These support timeout calibration questions, not an asserted system defect. Threads 348881/348973 add named LM Studio/LLM + UI/container conditions and NVRM memory errors, but the root causes and currently affected releases remain unclear.
risks: Deleting model files is destructive and should not be automated.
A blanket ban on Docker restart can affect intended service recovery.
Memory/OOM signals may be unavailable once the machine hard-freezes.
A long readiness grace can delay detection of a real startup deadlock; require progress evidence and a finite, workload-specific ceiling.

A container can be marked unhealthy because its healthcheck utility is absent, even when service state differs; validate the healthcheck command and service readiness before diagnosing OOM or applying a restart limit.
closure: Reproduce only in a disposable lab with explicit cgroup limits and restart=always container; verify whether host freezes, which OOM signals persist, and safe-mode recovery. Test an opt-in guard that disables just the offending service and preserves model data, then verify normal restart and rollback.

title: Keep a validated recovery path during headless first boot and platform updates
failure: Several early DGX Spark owners report boot hangs/loops after first setup or updates; one thread carries NVIDIA’s active stop-updating advisory and subsequent recovery notice. Recovery-media cases include USB mount failures on /dev/sda1, UEFI not enumerating media, and a report resolved by plugging the drive directly rather than through a hub. A different case needed package purge and booted the prior kernel. These reports may represent multiple independent incidents, and the initial setup/model installation correlation is unproven.
current_coverage: The kernel/initramfs update gate covers target kernel/module/initrd pairing before reboot. Existing HID and network recovery work tracks missing local/remote inputs, but does not verify recovery-media boot/mount on the exact OEM, document a last-known-good setup path, or distinguish USB hub/device enumeration from recovery image defects.
gap_or_complement: Extend update/OOBE preflight with a verifiable recovery-readiness check: record image version/hash, validate supported USB creation workflow and exact device identity instead of assuming /dev/sda1, confirm the recovery path is bootable on the target OEM before disruptive updates, and preserve a headless SSH/HID fallback. Follow current vendor advisories; never automate reflash or destructive package purge from an unverified symptom.
evidence_level: Medium that early units encountered real setup/boot/recovery failures (multiple owners and one official active-incident advisory); low for a shared root cause or general fix. Most reports are historical and hardware/software versions differ or are absent.
risks: Testing or recovery can erase data; use disposable/fully backed-up lab devices.
USB topology, secure boot keys and firmware differ by OEM and revision.
A generic blocker could prevent legitimate update/recovery workflows or leave headless owners without access.
The forum workaround to plug directly is one-user evidence, not a universal fix.
closure: On identified OEMs, reproduce supported OOBE/update/recovery flows with and without hubs and across supported media creators. Record OS/recovery image hash, BIOS/Secure Boot, kernel/driver, USB enumeration, boot logs, network/SSH and HID readiness. Include healthy negatives, an official known-issue advisory case, a prior-kernel fallback, and rollback/data-preservation evidence; verify any automation stops safely when the recovery path is absent.

title: Control thermal headroom consumed by idle unified-memory model residency
failure: One Spark owner reports repeatable sustained-load thermal-zone 92–97 C despite lower GPU-die temperatures; four models remained resident, three idle. Stopping the idle model containers reduced peak from 93–97 C to 83 C in the reported test and improved throughput. Other owners in the same 62-post thread report fan issues, thermal shutdown, dropped telemetry before shutdown and mixed Power Delivery firmware-bank versions, across different OEMs and unknown stacks. The thread is heterogeneous; no common cause or general driver/firmware fix is established.
current_coverage: Blackbox atom_gpu_telemetry samples all visible `/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp` zones every five seconds, GPU temperature/power, and thermal events; the current thermal mitigation is intentionally limited to named Blackbox batch jobs. FEATURE-FAN-RPM documents no reliable standard fan RPM on the local GB10. The collected host telemetry does not establish how many idle model-serving containers hold unified memory nor their incremental thermal load, and it does not safely stop shared vLLM/ComfyUI services. Its corroborated-event/mitigation gate also requires GPU power >=60 W; a real CPU/SoC/idle thermal event below that gate could be captured but excluded from this mitigation path. The forum’s long inference run does not provide GPU-rail watts, so it does not demonstrate an actual miss on this host.
gap_or_complement: Add a read-only correlation/admission report for active model/container residency, GPU rail power, per-zone thermal headroom, fan signal availability and workload concurrency before long runs. If evidence reproduces, make optional unloading of explicitly owned inactive containers or a workload-specific concurrency/clock cap an operator-confirmed action with bounded rollback. Prioritize vendor/OEM firmware disposition for shutdowns and exact PD FW1/FW2 differences; do not copy the forum SIGKILL-by-process-name watchdog.
evidence_level: Medium for one owner’s detailed before/after thermal-zone and resident-model measurements and multiple separate reports of fan/thermal faults; low for causality/generalization across OEMs, EC/PD firmware and ambient conditions. Attachments were not inspected.
risks: Unloading a container may terminate sessions or discard ephemeral state; require ownership and clean shutdown.
A thermal threshold derived from one unit/sensor mapping can false-stop healthy loads or react too late on another OEM.
Clock limits trade performance for margin and the claimed 2200 MHz mitigation is one-owner evidence.
The forum’s 60-second SIGKILL watchdog is not safe as-is: process-name matching can target unrelated processes, missing sensors default to no signal, and no hysteresis/owner check exists.
Power Delivery FW1/FW2 readings vary; interpreting them as failed or active banks requires OEM documentation before intervention.

A forum owner reports condensation when a thermoelectric cooler created a cold surface near the Spark; do not recommend TEC/AIO chassis modifications without dew-point/condensation and warranty validation.
closure: On identified GB10 OEM models and firmware, capture ambient, thermal-zone names/trip points and 5-second temperatures, GPU temperature/power/clocks, fan RPM where available, model/container residency, memory pressure and workload concurrency through repeated single-model versus multi-model idle-resident A/B and thermal soak. Prove unload behavior preserves active requests/data and restores service, test sensor missing/permission-denied and false-positive controls, and correlate any shutdown with kernel/pstore/OEM field diagnostics. Obtain vendor interpretation of exact PD FW1/FW2 versions before recommending firmware rollback/update or manual fan policy. Include a negative/control sweep around the 60 W GPU-power boundary with sustained CPU-only/SoC and idle-resident model loads. Confirm whether current corroboration drops a truly hot package event below that threshold before changing the gate, while retaining the tested anti-spike/debounce controls.

title: Capture scoped memory-test evidence without equating a small pass with GB10 memory health
failure: A DGX Spark owner reports memtester failures at large memory coverage while smaller tests sometimes pass; the standard DGX diagnostics directory and BMC interfaces are absent on Spark by design, complicating support escalation. A later 4G pass did not predict failures at 32G/64G.
current_coverage: No verified DGX Spark diagnostic suite is preinstalled and `nvsm show health` can lack a platform definition; BB does not run hardware memory stress tests or declare health from them. The relevant PDF, full memtester report and logs were attached but not inspected in this batch.
gap_or_complement: Consider an opt-in, bounded evidence receipt for an operator-run memtester/vendor-supported test: exact command, memtester version, allocation size/coverage and iterations, OS/kernel/OEM/BIOS/driver, start/end and process exit output, plus explicit `unknown` health when test range is incomplete. Do not run high-memory tests unattended, disturb resident workloads, or infer hardware replacement solely from memtester. Confirm with NVIDIA support which report/test is actually required before adding a bespoke diagnostics workflow.
evidence_level: Medium-low pending attachments: complete 12 human-post thread documents contradictory small/large test outcomes and official clarification that BMC/diagnostic suite are not part of Spark; no exact OEM firmware/driver or independent hardware diagnosis. PDF/screenshots not inspected.
risks: Memory tests consume substantial unified RAM and can trigger the host OOM/freeze path being studied in FEATURE-1358-CGROUP.
A 4G pass provides no evidence for untested physical ranges; a failure can also reflect application/tool instability rather than bad RAM.
Incorrectly presenting results as hardware health may cause unnecessary RMA or mask faults.
closure: Review the attached original memtester PDF/log and exact platform details; ask support for current DGX Spark-specific diagnostic requirement. In a disposable/test window, verify a limited collection receipt preserves command, covered size/ranges, exit status and unavailable diagnostic-suite/BMC fields without launching any stress test; ensure incomplete coverage always remains unknown.

title: Gate large-prefill workloads against delayed Spark hard resets
failure: A DGX Spark FE owner reports Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 crashes on first ~6.5k-token agentic prefill, exits container 255, then host hard-resets 2–3.5 minutes later without OOM/Xid or low MemAvailable. Same owner says Qwen3.6-35B MoE is stable on same stack; NVIDIA later RMA attributed diagnostics to a defective thermostat, so workload causality remains confounded.
current_coverage: CGROUP/recovery cards cover unified memory pressure and silent freezes; this thread adds a delayed reset after silent container failure and a dense-FP8 versus MoE comparison.
gap_or_complement: Record model precision/architecture, prefill size, active set, board/thermostat and power/thermal state; canary large prefills in steps, preserve known-good serving stack, and treat absent OOM/Xid as unknown cause rather than proof of safe capacity.
evidence_level: medium: complete seven-post thread, owner reports repeatability and contrast control; hardware later RMA makes root cause unresolved.
risks: Do not attribute hard reset to vLLM or model without distinguishing the RMA-reported thermostat fault.
No local reproduction or attachment inspection in this evidence batch.
closure: On exact OEM/firmware/driver, compare dense FP8 and MoE prefills while capturing external power/thermal/reset evidence; demonstrate delayed reset absent across soak and report could_not_run explicitly.

title: Exercise MTP remapping memory allocation under unified-memory pressure
failure: A dual-Spark owner observed NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY at _memdescAllocInternal during MTP shared-weight remapping; one occurrence continued serving, another prior event allegedly cascaded into RM locks and severe host hang. Another owner lost Qwen 397B after a vLLM Docker update due memory calculation and rolled back a repository tag. The maintainer suspected a recent vLLM memory accounting change; no fix/root cause was confirmed in the thread.
current_coverage: CGROUP work covers unified memory and recovery; runtime compatibility covers package/version gates. This adds MTP remap allocation timing and differentiation between recoverable allocation failure and fatal lock cascade.
gap_or_complement: Add a supported-stack canary that loads MTP/drafter alongside the main model, records free/charged system and CUDA memory before remap, and tests graceful refusal/rollback. Pin last known-good build until exact image/tag changes pass.
evidence_level: medium-low: full seven-post discussion, logs quoted by owner and maintainer acknowledgement; fatal cascade is an owner inference and cannot be tied to the nonfatal event.
risks: A single NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY is not evidence of imminent crash; avoid false-positive auto-restarts.
Old repo tags may have other security or compatibility regressions; rollback requires known-good inventory.
No attachment bundle or local reproduction reviewed.
closure: Reproduce on named driver/kernel/vLLM image, show allocation failure has bounded graceful recovery or identify/patch the fatal cascade, and validate with concurrent workload and soak.

title: Reject incompatible external KV cache connector and vLLM IPC versions before startup
failure: On a four-Spark setup, vLLM fork 0.11.2.dev plus LMCache 0.5.3 registered 170 hybrid KV tensors then hung wrapping them for IPC until 300s timeout. The thread author attributes this to an old fork IPC surface versus newer LMCache adapters; alternative hybrid-manager disablement demanded 160GB and could not fit. No host crash reported.
current_coverage: Runtime compatibility tracks exact framework/driver combinations; this adds the external KV connector and IPC adapter version contract.
gap_or_complement: Preflight connector/version/IPC adapter compatibility and perform an actual multi-node tensor registration smoke test before starting production service. Never infer compatibility from successful package install or cache registration alone.
evidence_level: medium: complete two-post report with stack versions and failure stage; suspected IPC incompatibility is author analysis, not confirmed upstream root cause.
risks: A compatibility gate may reject valid untested newer combinations; keep allowlist versioned and evidence-backed.
Disabling hybrid KV manager can exceed unified memory capacity; do not use as blind workaround.
closure: Reproduce exact fork/LMCache pair and show bounded startup failure; test a supported pair through registration, cache transfer and soak on two nodes.

title: Detect quality regressions when CPU OCR and GPU inference share GB10 UMA
failure: A DGX Spark owner reports table rows merging more frequently in CPU PaddlePaddle OCR when Ollama Llama 3.1 8B concurrently uses ~8–10GB GPU unified memory, compared with OCR at idle. A second participant says they built a Paddle GPU wheel for GX10, but no control/benchmark is supplied. The suggested NVLink-C2C/memory-bandwidth cause is unproven.
current_coverage: Existing admission proposal protects thermals and GPU progress; current forum thread exposes cross-device shared-memory bandwidth / application-quality interference and missing per-process bandwidth indicator.
gap_or_complement: Add paired OCR accuracy and latency acceptance under isolated versus concurrent LLM loads on exact GB10 stack. Admit, serialize or cap the competing workload only if the regression reproduces; do not claim numactl/cgroups solve bandwidth without measurement.
evidence_level: medium-low: complete two-post user observation with screenshots unread; correlation reported, proposed hardware cause not established, and no official NVIDIA response.
risks: Do not suppress useful parallel work on a single anecdote.
OCR extraction quality may depend on Paddle build, document, CPU load, or parsing configuration rather than unified-memory contention.
Screenshots and external wheel were not inspected.
closure: Run an exact-stack A/B across representative invoices with CPU OCR only, GPU inference only, and concurrent loads; report extraction metrics, CPU/GPU utilization, available UMA and any supported bandwidth counters. If regression is absent, close as not reproduced.

title: Validate checkpoint shard integrity, loader mode and OEM UMA headroom before serving
failure: A two-Spark Qwen3.5-397B AutoRound load hit duplicate safetensors key across shards with fastsafetensors; switching to regular safetensors resolved that specific error. The next configuration failed worker memory/Ray allocation (111 GiB available vs 112 GiB requested). Owner reports ASUS GX10 available memory differs from FE and firmware changed displayed capacity by ~2 GiB. No common root cause or verified production workload is established.
current_coverage: Runtime compat tracks exact model/runtime pairs; unified memory proposals cover OOM. This adds manifest/index/shard integrity and OEM-specific reserved-memory budget at checkpoint admission.
gap_or_complement: Before launch, validate index keys are unique and match shard contents, pin loader mode and exact framework image, measure available UMA after boot on each OEM/firmware, and reject a requested allocation above the observed budget with actionable headroom. Include declared auxiliary/MTP tensors in the manifest-to-checkpoint coverage check and compare config counts with actual shard tensors before admitting a model; test the exact quant/export path and preserve a known-good checkpoint.
evidence_level: medium: complete 14-post troubleshooting thread with commands/errors and owner workaround; diagnosis around available-memory variation is community explanation, not verified firmware causal test. The 139-post PrismaQuant thread reports a related producer-side completeness failure: a fine-tune retained MTP tensors while its config omitted the MTP layer count, causing the external quantizer’s shard scheduler to omit weights; a downstream validation then rejected export. The author proposed deriving count from actual weights, but the repo change and fix were not audited. Treat as a checkpoint/auxiliary-weight completeness probe for an exact artifact; it does not show BB’s own loader is affected.
risks: Regular safetensors may load more slowly than fastsafetensors; include time/capacity tradeoff in canary.
Do not reclaim reserved memory or remove system services solely to satisfy an oversized request.
External shard artifacts not downloaded/inspected and thread screenshots unread.
closure: Reproduce the duplicate-key error from an exact checkpoint hash, show integrity gate catches it, then compare both loaders with measured UMA on exact OEM firmware; prove launch either fits with declared margin or exits before damaging host usability.

title: Require a versioned stability soak for Nemotron 3 Super vLLM serving

title: Treat passing FieldDiag MemStress as bounded evidence, not memory integrity proof

A pass/fail instrument disagreement must not automatically trigger memory remapping or host quarantine without OEM policy.
False confidence from PASS can expose users to further corruption; false RMA from userspace test can disrupt service.
closure: Reproduce on exact GX10 firmware/kernel using supported memory stress plus OS mapping checks, capture both full logs; demonstrate which layer fails and document the OEM escalation threshold. Until then return `unknown` on conflicting results.

title: Preserve a GSP-failure escalation path when display, UEFI and FieldDiag are unavailable
failure: A DGX Spark FE on OS7.5/kernel6.17.0-1021/driver580.159.03 reported repeated Xid119/SEC2 GSP init timeout (expected GSP_INIT_DONE; RmInitAdapter failed), with PCI device enumerated but `nvidia-smi` unavailable after OTA. current_coverage: GSP boot health card separates PCI enumeration from GSP/CUDA readiness and has recovery/diagnostic controls; rescue runbook notes Spark lacks BMC/out-of-band management. This supplies a confirmed recovery-persistence and diagnostic-access failure chain.

risks: A failed recovery plus no console/SSH can make the unit unrecoverable remotely; no BMC path is reported for Spark.
Disabling Secure Boot to force unsigned MODS may violate policy and is not a confirmed fix.
Do not infer that forced power-off caused the GSP failure from temporal association.
Full recovery erases the SSD; only use after evidence capture/approved data handling.
RMA data custody/sanitization can conflict with no-display/UEFI access; preserve data handling plan before lockout and confirm OEM rules rather than assuming SSD retention is allowed.
closure: On a sacrificial/canary FE, test GSP timeout detection and recovery escalation without changing Secure Boot; verify logs remain available through SSH when possible, that no-video/no-SSH failure routes to OEM/RMA, and define approved SSD sanitization/custody steps before return.

title: Escalate persistent PCIe data-path write failures instead of repeating destructive recovery
failure: A DGX Spark FE reported recurrent NVMe write transfer errors (SCT 0 / SC 4), ext4 journal abort/read-only remount, changing failed LBAs, clean SMART and PCIe DOE mailbox timeout/x0-width indications. Small writes and mkfs sometimes passed while sustained/recovery-image writes failed. Two official recovery attempts did not restore a bootable system; FieldDiag FioSSD failed while GPU/CPU/thermal tests passed, and NVIDIA said it qualified for RMA. evidence_level: high: complete 7-post thread with repeated boot/write behavior, two recovery attempts, FieldDiag summary and explicit NVIDIA RMA eligibility; full binary logs not inspected and GPU/NVMe shared-path causality is unverified.
risks: Recovery/install may further corrupt filesystem or erase user data while writes are failing.
A clean SMART report does not validate the PCIe data path.
The reported x0 PCIe/DOE lines may be normal on some units per another user; use correlated write failures/FioSSD failure, not that line alone, for RMA diagnosis.

title: Gate patched M-RoPE kernel and CUDA-graph vision soak on exact SM121 stack

Third-party patched SGLang image and kernel have no verified upstream/OEM support; no production adoption.

title: Gate structured output and tool-call transitions with speculative decoding
failure: On community vLLM 0.22.1rc1 and 0.23.1rc1, Qwen3.6 tool/structured-output generation intermittently hit xgrammar FSM failures and terminated requests with HTTP 500. A PR enabling grammars for default auto tool-choice paths was partially reverted; maintainer says transition bugs remain for advanced models with speculative decoding and reasoning→tool boundaries. Setting VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=false reduced errors but also disabled output guidance and led to invalid JSON. Removing MTP resolved one user’s specific failures, not all scenarios.
current_coverage: Runtime compatibility card requires exact model/runtime pairing and functional smoke tests; this adds structured schema/tool transition probes with and without MTP and strict enforcement.
gap_or_complement: Before promoting vLLM updates, run multi-turn reasoning→tool transitions, tool_choice auto/required, strict and non-strict schemas, JSON nested arrays/enums, and speculative decode on the exact recipe. Preserve strict safety contracts; do not treat suppressing xgrammar errors as a correct fix if output becomes invalid.
evidence_level: high for request failures and partial upstream revert: complete 15-post thread, maintainer response, user confirms initial fix and later residual failures. The exact patch/commit was not independently fetched or tested locally. Complementary 86-post MiMo-V2.5/DFlash thread: one operator documents structured/tool calls terminated by grammar rejection under outlines and failures with KiloCode; another operator reports the same setup works with default xgrammar and identifies outlines EOS rejection as the 500 trigger. This disagreement narrows the gate to exact backend/template/client combinations; community patches and their claims remain unaudited.
risks: HTTP 500 breaks user requests; disabling constraints can silently produce invalid JSON or violate downstream contracts.
Removing MTP may affect latency/capacity but does not alone prove correctness across other schemas.
Regression may affect multiple models at reasoning/schema boundaries, not only Qwen3.6.
closure: Test exact before/after vLLM commit across listed request transitions with MTP on/off; show no grammar termination and schema validity for strict cases, and verify the fix preserves constraints rather than suppressing them.

title: Keep a validated HDMI console attached during firmware and reboot sequences

title: Classify low GPU power by workload and power-state evidence before treating it as a fault
failure: A GX10 owner reports only 60W GPU draw/65 TFLOPS on a max-GPU benchmark and interprets the SW Power Capping counter as a fixed firmware ceiling. NVIDIA clarified the published 140W is total GB10 SoC CPU+GPU TDP, not a guaranteed GPU-only draw, and requested exact workload, adapter, DMI firmware, `nvidia-smi -q -d POWER` capture and FieldDiag. Another owner reports a similar degraded state that full unplug restored. The first author has no posted outcome.

gap_or_complement: Represent state as expected-under-workload, degraded-suspected, or unknown; correlate throughput/clock/utilization/power/throttle counters with CPU+GPU load and exact OEM firmware. Do not issue resets from low GPU watts alone. When degraded state persists, capture DMI, power samples and FieldDiag before approved full AC cycle/RMA route.
evidence_level: medium: complete 10-post thread including explicit NVIDIA clarification and requested diagnostics; author supplied no follow-up logs and community cause remains open.
risks: GPU watts alone below 140W can be normal because the published limit is SoC-wide and workload-dependent.
Unnecessary AC cycle interrupts active team workloads and may lose evidence.
A real latched power state can still evade diagnosis if only idle snapshots are recorded.
closure: On exact GX10 workload profiles, establish expected power/clock ranges under GPU-only and mixed CPU+GPU load; test capture distinguishes a community-reported degraded state from normal operation, preserving `unknown` if evidence cannot separate them.

title: Keep unified-memory allocation admission fail-closed on near-capacity vLLM loads
failure: A public community GLM-5 NVFP4 recipe patches vLLM worker memory validation so `free_memory < requested_memory` becomes a warning followed by continuing startup, on four nodes with `gpu_memory_utilization=0.98`, context pushes toward 100K, small KV budget, and several system services disabled. The author says the setup may be unstable at large context. This bypass is not upstream, not locally validated and may let an overcommitted UMA process proceed toward kernel/driver OOM.

gap_or_complement: Do not carry this patch into BB. Preserve fail-closed admission when measured free memory is below request; if a supported workload is rejected, investigate accounting with diagnostics and calibrate a bounded OEM-specific budget rather than overriding the check. Canary any approved change under system/service memory pressure and concurrency with a recoverable prior stack.
evidence_level: high that the recipe explicitly bypasses the check, based on complete 19-post thread and exact patch snippet; resulting instability/OOM risk is inferred, not reported as a reproduced host crash. External repository was not reviewed.
risks: Continuing under a known shortfall can create kernel OOM, wedged GPU allocations, loss of SSH/remote recovery or hard reset.
Disabling system services and dropping caches can mask rather than fix budget error.
Do not generalize user-reported memory totals across FE/GX10/Lenovo firmware.
closure: Keep the memory check enabled; reproduce supported model within budget and show rejected loads exit before host stress. If a vendor-supported admission correction is needed, require real UMA accounting and pressure/soak plus rollback validation.

title: Detect and gate silent NCCL fallback from NET/IB to TCP on GB10 multi-node runs
gap: La receta de compatibilidad actual no verifica que el plugin NCCL elegido realmente registró memoria y abrió transporte RDMA compatible con UMA GB10; en el reporte AWS OFI falla ibv_reg_mr_iova2/DMABUF GDR aunque NCCL_IB_DISABLE no evita el intento, dejando ejecución por TCP. El hilo 366147 aporta un timeout ALLREDUCE tardío bajo DDP con hipótesis de proxy CPU NCCL/SIGSEGV frente a una explicación de heartbeat/HCA no reproducida; el gate de runtime necesita un soak largo y separar esos mecanismos antes de escoger transporte o knobs. El hilo 366373 añade a MSI EdgeXpert un cambio reportado de 3.0→16.2 GB/s al bindear rails y 24.3 GB/s tras otra ronda que mezcló actualización LVFS-testing con doble rail; sin versiones/componentes exactos, la mejora no se puede adjudicar al firmware.
proposal: En el smoke test multi-nodo registrar plugin, transporte efectivo y benchmark NCCL all_gather sobre la configuración/OEM/kernel/driver exactos. Si NET/IB no se inicializa, clasificar como degradación o could_not_run y evitar declarar lista la ruta; evaluar NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none solo como canary exacto para permitir plugin IB integrado. No imponer variable global ni atribuir el límite al PCIe Gen1 x1 del endpoint GPU, que NVIDIA explica como C2C esperado.
confidence: media: el usuario aporta logs y repetición en dos FE; NVIDIA confirma la topología de puertos y progreso reportado, pero los adjuntos no fueron revisados y no hay réplica local. En el caso DDP la explicación del proxy es análisis de un usuario, hay una interpretación alternativa y el autor no informa resultado definitivo; no adoptar `TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC` o ajustes HCA sin medir la reproducción exacta.
risks: Deshabilitar el plugin externo puede quitar transportes optimizados de otras plataformas; el fallback puede alterar rendimiento/estabilidad multi-nodo. Resultado de banda varía con puertos, fabric y payload.
closure: En FE con versiones citadas y control de plugin, reproducir fallo/fallback, comparar TCP vs NET/IB con 1 y 2 NICs, verificar throughput/errores y repetir con otra configuración no afectada; confirmar que gate informa desconocido cuando logs/transporte no se pueden leer. Incluir rollback de variables y validar en otro OEM antes de generalizar. Añadir un soak DDP/multi-node prolongado con contador de colectivas y logs rank para reproducir la firma; comparar transportes únicamente en configuración soportada y no inferir que GDR=0 causa la falla. Repetir secuencialmente baseline/rail binding en firmware oficial, luego solo si OEM lo soporta comparar firmware nuevo, registrar versiones y canales; retirar `lvfs-testing` del remote tras canary y confirmar estado persistente/rollback. Evitar confundir un test que falla por `libnccl.so.2` faltante con rendimiento del transporte.

title: Keep thermal and power-loss incidents open when the installed diagnostic stack cannot run
gap: Un estado dcgmi health HEALTHY puede coexistir con una suite incompleta: DCGM 3.3.9 no admite CUDA 13.0 y SysMon no carga; en el mismo hilo hubo power-off físico a los seis minutos de FieldDiag PowerStress. La ficha térmica no debe tratar telemetría disponible o pruebas parciales como exclusión de fallo térmico/eléctrico/hardware.
proposal: Verificar compatibilidad de DCGM/FieldDiag con CUDA, driver y OEM antes del ensayo; representar cada prueba no ejecutada como could_not_run y mantener el incidente abierto ante apagado físico sin causa. Separar la recomendación NVIDIA de RMA para FE del governor comunitario: tratar enfriamiento/frecuencia solo como canary temporal con telemetría externa y stop criteria, nunca como fix probado. Capturar adaptador, ambiente, carga, temperaturas, cambios y serial para soporte.
confidence: media: relato detallado de dos equipos y respuesta de NVIDIA indicando RMA para FE; mejora tras separar/gobernar no causal, y captura adjunta sin revisar.
risks: Umbrales térmicos expuestos pueden no cubrir hotspots; un límite preventivo puede bajar capacidad sin corregir defecto. Una batería de pruebas incompatible puede dar falsa tranquilidad.
closure: En stack/OEM exactos, validar que la selección de DCGM/FieldDiag ejecuta cada módulo o marca fallo de compatibilidad, nunca PASS global; ensayar PowerStress en banco recuperable con PSU y ambiente registrados. Criterio de apagado debe dirigir a ticket/RMA según fabricante; comprobar que canary térmico reversible no sustituye esa escalación.

title: Block FieldDiag DOCA-OFED prerequisites that replace the Spark inbox ConnectX-7 driver stack
gap: La guía FieldDiag 2.x citada pide instalar doca-ofed/kernel-mft-dkms en Spark aunque DGX OS release notes citadas declaran inbox OFED y sin soporte doca-ofed; apt sustituyó `mlx5_core` por DKMS no firmado, dejando CX7 sin driver y cortando RoCE. La rutina actual debe detectar esa transacción antes de la instalación, incluso si no remueve los metapaquetes `nvidia-system-*`.
proposal: Antes de ejecutar pre-requisitos FieldDiag sobre Spark, comprobar modelo/OEM y simular la transacción APT; rechazar o requerir revisión si `doca-ofed`, `mlnx-ofed-kernel-dkms` o `kernel-mft-dkms` reemplazan `nvidia-mlnx-tools`, `rdma-core`/verbs inbox o módulos mlx5 integrados/signed. Mantener acceso/rescate y un rollback verificado. Confirmar guía/versiones con NVIDIA; no recomendar `ofed_uninstall.sh --force` ni copiar la receta comunitaria de purge. El post posterior informa que instalar `nvidia-mlnx-tools` restauró CX7 en un caso, pero la versión/pinning varía.
confidence: media-alta para el fallo reportado: comparación pareada de unidad afectada y peer sano con mismo kernel y CX7 firmware, segundo usuario confirma y NVIDIA acepta reparación propuesta. Sin inspección independiente del PDF o artifacts, y el autor original acabó solicitando RMA sin causalidad final.
risks: Cambios DOCA/MFT pueden eliminar metapaquetes de plataforma, módulos firmados e interfaces de red; rollback genérico puede purgar dependencias críticas o dejar apt atado a versiones que ya cambiaron. El soporte depende de OEM, DGX OS y FieldDiag exactos.
closure: En copia/lab de FE DGX OS/kernel citados, guardar simulado de instalación y confirmar que gate lo detiene antes de modificar paquetes; probar fixture inocuo y control negativo con stack inbox intacto. Validar el procedimiento oficialmente soportado de CX7Stress o mantener CX7Stress deshabilitado sin romper clustering. Cualquier recuperación debe preservar apt sources/pins y probar mlx5 bound, `/sys/class/infiniband`, cuatro netdevs y conectividad después de reinicio; verificar rollback seguro.

title: Validate advertised model context and colocated UMA budget before auto-restarting model containers
gap: A model config whose `max_position_embeddings` is below requested `--max-model-len` can fail at startup; with Docker `--restart unless-stopped` the invalid configuration is reported to loop. A separate report shows model plus embedding init exceeds 121GB UMA despite each workload loading alone; cgroup RSS/docker stats can understate CUDA memory.
proposal: Before starting an auto-restarting inference container, compare requested context with model config and check a workload-local UMA budget for resident weights, KV cache, graph/init peaks, embedding services and desktop/host reserve. Fail closed with explicit reason on invalid context or overcommitted admission; keep restart count/backoff bounded and preserve model/cache data. Treat the reported Nemotron/Qwen numbers as version- and recipe-specific examples, not safe universal thresholds.
confidence: media: detailed owner-maintained benchmark/stack and explicit observed init failure are reported, but no raw log/fixture attached and the 512K loop is presented as recipe guidance without standalone reproduced output.
risks: Model config can misstate operational context; estimated memory may omit allocator/graph peaks. A strict rule can block a workload that would fit at smaller context or concurrency. Restart policy may be managed externally.
closure: Build fixtures for valid context, over-limit context, duplicate heavy services over UMA, unknown model metadata and working control; verify preflight denies unsafe cases with status and does not launch a retry loop. Canary against exact OEM/driver/container/model, record actual peak UMA and effective context, test recovery/backoff and rollback. Ensure missing CUDA memory evidence stays unknown.

title: Distinguish MT7925 pairwise-key installation failure and 5 GHz roam loops from wrong-password or host failure
gap: La UI y supplicant pueden presentar `WRONG_KEY` aunque 4-way WPA exchange derive claves y `nl80211 NEW_KEY` falle con `-2 ENOENT`; NetworkManager no es la causa al reproducirse con wpa_supplicant directo. Otro GX10 con el mismo MT7925e/kernel pierde 5 GHz en loops de beacon/regulatory state mientras 2.4 GHz fijado aparece estable. El actual error de Wi-Fi-isolation debe distinguir autenticación real, driver key-install, band-specific link loss y host health.
proposal: Correlacionar supplicant key-install/ENOENT, cipher, AP/BSSID/band, driver/firmware/kernel y NetworkManager state con probe local y management endpoint; mostrar la causa de infraestructura sin pedir PSK repetidamente. Una actualización de kernel no fue fix para el MSI citado aunque actualizó 1021 a 1026; el autor de GX10 reporta 2.4 GHz/BSSID como workaround y `disable_clc=1` incompleto para 5GHz. Mantener fallback Ethernet/management; no fijar canales, BSSID ni módulo driver globalmente antes de A/B y validar OEM.
